summary: Michel Mohr is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Geneva, where he was an assistant (1987–1992), and held posts at Hanazono University (attested 2000–2006) and the University of Hawaii (attested 2008–2012).

Michel Strickmann (1942–1994) worked in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied under teachers including Hulsewé, Zürcher, Vos, Kaltenmark, Stein, Schipper, and Vandermeersch, completing his PhD at Paris Diderot University. He held positions at UC Berkeley, Bordeaux, and Wissenschaftskolleg zu Berlin.

Michela Clemente is a scholar of Tibetology. She studied under Elena De Rossi Filibeck and Hildegard Diemberger (2013–2015), and held a post as a Marie Sklodowska Curie Fellow at the University of Cambridge.
Michele Kerbaker (1835–1914) worked in Indology and linguistics. He succeeded Giacomo Lignana in 1870 and held a post at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" from circa 1872 to 1907.

Michelle C. Wang works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. She studied under Eugene Y. Wang (~2003–2008) and became an assistant professor in the Department of Art and Art History at Georgetown University circa 2012.

Michelle Spuler (born 1971) specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Queensland and taught at Colorado College and in the Department of Religious Studies at Victoria University of Wellington.

Michihiko Komine (born 1945) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University. He served there as an assistant (attested 1978–1980) and professor (attested 2014–2015), and was board chairman of the Japanese Association for Esoteric Buddhist Studies (attested 2015).

Michihiko Yajima (born 1963) is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied as a graduate student at the University of Tokyo (attested 1981) and held posts there (attested 1992) and as a professor at Tsurumi University (attested 2003–2008).

Michihiro Ikeda works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held instructor posts at Setagaya Gakuen High School (attested 1996) and Komazawa Junior College (attested 2005), and served as a librarian at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2005).

Michiko Yusa (born 1951) is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology. She completed her PhD at the University of California, Santa Barbara under Raimon Panikkar (~1978–1983) and became a professor of foreign languages at Western Washington University (~1983).
Michio Kamikawa (born 1960) specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Ritsumeikan University (~1979–1989) and held a post at Aichi Prefectural University circa 2005.

Michio Yano (born 1944) works in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1963–1972) and Brown University under David Pingree (~1978–1980), and served as a professor at Kyoto Sangyo University (~1974–2010).

Michitoshi Barada works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Jien Abe and J. R. Joshi, as well as at Savitribai Phule Pune University (1997), and held research posts at Otani University (attested 1992) and the Eastern Institute (attested 2000–2003).
Michiya Ito studied as a graduate student at Tohoku University (attested 1986–1990) and later held a post there (attested 2001–2004).
Michiyo Hoshi (born 1941) is a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. She held posts at the Research Institute for Languages and Cultures of Asia and Africa and at Toyo Bunko (attested 2003).
Midori Nishino is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed doctoral studies at Taisho University (attested 2006) and later worked there as a researcher (attested 2010–2015).

Migmar Tsering (1956–1999) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Khenpo Appey Rinpoche. He served as a Sa skya expert at CIHTS (attested 1990), head of Sakya College (attested 1991–1997), and at TASS (attested 2006).

Mikaël Bauer works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Kanazawa University under Paul Hoornaert and Noritoshi Aramaki, and earned his PhD at Harvard University under Ryuichi Abe (attested 2010).

Mikel Burley works in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Essex and the University of Bristol (PhD 2005) under supervisors including John Peacock, and became an Associate Professor of Religion and Philosophy at the University of Leeds.
Mikio Otsuki works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He has held positions as a research fellow at Manpuku-ji (attested 2007) and as a professor at Hanazono University (attested 2007).
